title: Supporting Productivity Skill Development in College Students through Social Robot Coaching: A Proof-of-Concept
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to support college students who struggle with productivity-related skills such as time management and task prioritization. The authors argue that common supports like productivity apps and self-help books are limited because they are either not educational, not personalized, or not scalable, while human coaching can be effective but resource-intensive. The study asks whether a socially assistive robot (SAR) can serve as a scalable educational coach for productivity skill development in higher education.

The intervention is a proof-of-concept robotic coaching system built around QTrobot and GPT-4. Students interact through a text chat interface while the robot responds with speech and gestures. The system begins with an introductory conversation to identify students’ productivity challenges and preferences, then recommends and delivers six lessons on time management and task prioritization strategies: time blocking, time tracking, task breakdown, the Eisenhower matrix, the ABCDE method, and Eat That Frog. A dashboard tracks progress, mood, time spent, self-reported confidence, engagement, and personalized productivity insights.

The study was conducted with 15 undergraduate students aged 18–24 who were screened for challenges in time management or plan management using the Executive Skills Questionnaire-Revised. Sessions took place in a meeting room at the local institute, with each session lasting about 60 minutes. Data collection included quantitative usability and Likert-scale ratings as well as qualitative open-ended feedback about the interface, dashboard, and robot coaching experience.

The main conclusions are that the SAR-based coaching system showed promising usability, engagement, and perceived relevance for productivity support. Participants rated the system highly on usability (SUS = 79.2) and generally found the lessons helpful, especially for task prioritization. Many appreciated the robot’s social presence, personalization options, and dashboard-based feedback. However, this was an early proof-of-concept evaluation without a control group, using a small and somewhat skewed sample, so the findings mainly support feasibility and user acceptance rather than strong causal claims about learning effectiveness.

identified_tools.name: QTrobot
identified_tools.description: A socially assistive robot platform by LuxAI that supports speech, gestures, and facial expressions for human-robot interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the embodied productivity coach delivering six lessons on time management and task prioritization to college students through a chat-and-speech interface, with dashboard-based progress and reflection features.

findings.finding_summary: Participants reported the coaching was helpful for productivity-related soft skills, especially task prioritization and time management. Coaching helpfulness for task prioritization was rated Mean=4.53±0.88 and for time management Mean=4.00±0.73 on 5-point Likert scales; 73% rated task-prioritization coaching as very helpful, while 67% rated time-management coaching as somewhat helpful and 20% very helpful.
findings.measure: Participant ratings of coaching helpfulness for task prioritization and time management on 5-point Likert scales

findings.finding_summary: Lesson relevance was rated positively, suggesting the robot-delivered instruction aligned with participants' needs. Lesson relevance was Mean=4.40±1.02 on a 5-point Likert scale; 9 of 15 participants strongly agreed the lessons were relevant, 5 somewhat agreed, and 1 somewhat disagreed.
findings.measure: Participant ratings of lesson relevance on a 5-point Likert scale

findings.finding_summary: The system demonstrated high usability in this proof-of-concept evaluation. The System Usability Scale score was 79.2, above the benchmark average of 68 and corresponding to an 'A-' grade; interface usability was also rated Mean=4.87±0.34.
findings.measure: System Usability Scale (SUS) and interface usability ratings

findings.finding_summary: Participants reported positive overall experience and engagement with the robot-based coaching system. Average ratings were 4.3 out of 5 for overall experience and 4.2 out of 5 for engagement; additionally, 60% felt the robot helped them stay engaged throughout the session.
findings.measure: Post-experiment ratings of overall experience, engagement, and robot contribution to engagement

findings.finding_summary: Perceptions of the robot's contribution were positive overall but varied across participants. Robot contribution to coaching effectiveness was rated Mean=3.40±1.50 and contribution to coaching engagement Mean=3.67±1.53 on 5-point Likert scales; 53% somewhat or strongly agreed its presence made coaching more effective, while some participants found speech or gestures distracting.
findings.measure: Participant ratings of robot contribution to coaching effectiveness and engagement on 5-point Likert scales

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language model used for generating conversational responses and personalized analyses.
identified_tools.use_case: Used via prompt engineering on GPT-4 to power the robot's productivity-coaching dialogue, tailor lesson sequencing and examples, classify mood, and generate personalized productivity insights.

findings.finding_summary: The GPT-4-powered coaching content was perceived as relevant and helpful for productivity skill development. Participants rated lesson relevance at Mean=4.40±1.02, coaching helpfulness for time management at Mean=4.00±0.73, and coaching helpfulness for task prioritization at Mean=4.53±0.88.
findings.measure: Participant ratings of lesson relevance and coaching helpfulness for time management and task prioritization

findings.finding_summary: Participants reported that the LLM-based coaching felt personalized and context-aware, citing examples where the system adapted explanations to their background and goals. Overall experience averaged 4.3 out of 5 and engagement 4.2 out of 5.
findings.measure: Post-experiment ratings and qualitative feedback on personalization, overall experience, and engagement

findings.finding_summary: The GPT-4-based system supported a highly usable coaching workflow overall, but some interaction limitations remained. The overall SUS score was 79.2, yet some participants described the advice as too theoretical and reported fatigue from typing responses, which reduced engagement.
findings.measure: System Usability Scale (SUS) and qualitative feedback on interaction quality

quality_tier_rationale: This is a proof-of-concept study with 15 participants using post-session surveys, descriptive statistics, and qualitative feedback, but no control group, randomization, or pre/post causal outcome design. The evidence is therefore mixed-methods/usability-oriented rather than rigorous causal evaluation.
impact_tier_rationale: Results are positive on usability, engagement, and perceived helpfulness, but no standardized learning gains or causal effect sizes are reported. Impact appears promising but remains unclear in magnitude.
